description: Lines drawing themselves on and being erased, over a colour bed with nothing on disk. Top: a straight arrow whose `shape.trim_end` runs 0 → 1 over frames 0–20. Middle: an S-curved arrow doing the same. Right: a ring (an ellipse) whose `shape.trim_start` runs 0 → 0.5, so it is erased clockwise from its rightmost point. Frame 0: no arrows at all — not even a head — and the whole ring. Frame 10: each arrow half drawn from its start, its head riding the drawn end (the straight one's tip at mid-run, the S's tip at the middle of the S, pointing along the curve there, which is diagonal down-right), and the ring missing the quarter from its rightmost point clockwise round to its bottom. Frame 20: both arrows whole with heads at their ends, and only the ring's upper half (from its leftmost point clockwise over the top to its rightmost). What a wrong render looks like: a head at the far end on frame 0 or 10 means the head does not ride the trim; the S's drawn half ending well short of or past its middle means the trim is by curve parameter rather than by distance; the ring missing a different quarter means the outline starts somewhere else or runs the other way; frames 0, 10 and 20 identical means a keyframed shape was drawn once for the whole segment.
